subject.title: Codex app-server client closes before long maintenance turn completes; Gateway restart also terminates active turn without graceful recovery

question: For Codex-backed turns interrupted after possible side effects, should OpenClaw resume the turn, synthesize a final status after restart, or fail closed with restart-specific guidance?
rationale: Current source has partial retry and restart-marker mechanisms, but choosing the remaining behavior crosses replay safety, Codex transport failure classification, Gateway lifecycle, and channel delivery policy.

options.title: Design restart-aware recovery
options.body: Define a single cross-surface policy for Gateway shutdown, unexpected app-server close, safe resume, and final user-visible follow-up, then implement it with focused tests.

options.title: Improve classification only
options.body: Keep runtime behavior fail-closed but make user-facing messages and logs distinguish Gateway restart from unexpected app-server failure.

options.title: Wait for live reproduction
options.body: Keep this open under live-repro until a current-main run proves the remaining long-maintenance failure trigger.

recommendation.title: Design restart-aware recovery
recommendation.body: Define a single cross-surface policy for Gateway shutdown, unexpected app-server close, safe resume, and final user-visible follow-up, then implement it with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the bounded Codex retry boundary and contributed heavily to the adjacent restart recovery path, making them the strongest routing owner for the product policy.
